newsitem.title: UK: British minister dismisses ERM entry rumours.
newsitem.headline: British minister dismisses ERM entry rumours.

text.p: The minister in charge of government information on Friday dismissed rumours that Britain's new Labour government was planning eventual re-entry for sterling into the European Union's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
Minister without portfolio Peter Mandelson told Sky television: "I really would not pay any attention to that sort of City rumour or press speculation."

"I can assure you categorically that these rumours were not based on any information at all from Number 10 or Number 11 Downing Street (residences of Prime Minister Tony Blair and Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown)," Mandelson added.
A news agency report suggesting Britain might rejoin the ERM in 2001 with the central rate for sterling at 2.50 marks caused a sharp fall in the pound on Thursday.
It recovered slightly overnight, and was trading around 2.7740 marks at 0730 GMT.
